package_info.package_name: Magecart credit card skimmer (First Aid Beauty site)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (site infection, not a versioned package)
package_info.why_malicious: The Magecart skimmer is malicious because it consists of heavily obfuscated and encrypted JavaScript code injected into the checkout page of a legitimate e-commerce website. Its purpose is to surreptitiously steal credit card information from users during the payment process, specifically targeting US-based victims on Windows systems. The stolen payment data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure, resulting in direct financial theft and privacy compromise.

execution_context.trigger: When the user submits the payment form during checkout
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript within the checkout/payment page of the First Aid Beauty website
required_permissions: Access to the DOM (to read payment form fields)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user submits the payment form during checkout, the code accesses the credit card number field from the DOM, creates an XMLHttpRequest, and sends the extracted credit card data via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded external attacker-controlled domain, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code is suspicious because it is obfuscated, executes specifically during the payment process, and exfiltrates sensitive credit card data to an external domain that is not associated with the legitimate merchant. The use of obfuscation and hardcoded external endpoints is a strong indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce site JavaScript should never collect and transmit raw credit card data to unknown or undocumented third-party domains, especially using obfuscated or encrypted code. Payment data should only be handled by trusted, PCI-compliant payment processors with transparent, auditable code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate payment processors or analytics scripts may collect form data, but only to trusted, documented endpoints and with clear, unobfuscated code. Such scripts are typically reviewed and authorized by the merchant and do not transmit sensitive data to unrecognized domains.
key_indicators: Heavily obfuscated and/or encrypted JavaScript injected into payment pages
Direct access to payment form fields (e.g., credit card number, CVV) via DOM methods
Network requests (e.g., XMLHttpRequest or fetch) sending payment data to hardcoded, untrusted external domains
Execution triggered specifically by payment form submission events
Targeting of specific geolocations (e.g., US) and operating systems (e.g., Windows) to evade detection

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is injected into the checkout/payment page of the First Aid Beauty site.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimmer code in the browser of site visitors.

attack_chain.action: When a user submits the payment form, the skimmer code collects credit card data from the DOM.
attack_chain.leads_to: Preparation of sensitive data for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: The collected credit card data is sent via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of payment information to the attacker.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated or encrypted JavaScript accessing payment form fields during checkout
JavaScript code sending payment data (credit card number, CVV, etc.) to external, non-payment domains
Runtime DOM scraping of sensitive fields immediately before or during form submission events
Presence of scripts that execute only for specific geolocations or user agents (e.g., US Windows users)
file_indicators: Injected or appended JavaScript code within the checkout/payment page HTML
Unusual <script> tags or inline event handlers not present in the legitimate site codebase
Presence of obfuscated or minified code blocks that are not part of the official site scripts
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests from client browsers to domains not associated with the merchant (e.g., https://malicious-domain.com/collect)
Outbound traffic containing credit card number patterns or other payment data to unrecognized external endpoints
Network requests initiated at the moment of payment form submission to suspicious domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor e-commerce site pages for unauthorized or obfuscated JavaScript, especially code that accesses payment form fields and sends data to unknown external domains. Use web application firewalls (WAFs) to block or alert on suspicious outbound requests containing payment data. Regularly audit site code and third-party scripts for unauthorized changes or injections. Implement network monitoring to detect POST requests containing credit card data sent to non-payment domains, and correlate with form submission events for high-fidelity detection.
